title: Field sprint spin-up: Acadia outage retrospective (Nov 2027)
content:
Summary:

This note captures the postmortem-style retrospective from the Nov 1–3 field sprint at Acadia Corp (on‑prem VPC-connected cluster). Team responded to repeated customer-visible model load failures and intermittent network blackholes that blocked their production traffic. This is a working capture — action items and runbook edits below.

Attendees:
- Priya Nair (owner)
- Carlos Mendes (network lead)
- Ava Chen (SRE)
- Jonah Patel (install engineer)
- Elena Gomez (customer success, Acadia liaison)
- On-call: SRE shift B

High-level timeline (condensed):
- 2027-11-01 08:20 UTC: Customer pager — model load errors observed (pods crash repeated during startup).
- 2027-11-01 09:00 UTC: Triage call; initial hypothesis: corrupted model artifacts (S3-access).
- 2027-11-01 11:15 UTC: Reproduce: model load succeeds locally; fails from within customer subnet.
- 2027-11-01 14:40 UTC: Network team reproduces intermittent packet drops between worker nodes and their NAT gateway.
- 2027-11-02 02:30 UTC: Hotfix deployed: pin kernel offload settings, increase NAT conntrack timeouts. Immediate customer throughput improved but occasional flaps persisted.
- 2027-11-03 10:00 UTC: Root cause identified and validated (see below). Final mitigation plan agreed.

Observed customer impact:
- API error spikes (502/504) during peak model load windows — visible to three internal product teams.
- Longer-than-expected cold start times for model shards (~40–120s vs expected 8–20s) causing request timeouts and retries.
- Customers temporarily disabled a critical data pipeline to avoid cost/rate penalties.

Root cause (validated):
- Primary cause: MTU mismatch between Acadia's edge switch fabric and our appliance NICs when jumbo frames were enabled on fabric. This created recurring fragmentation and alignment faults for certain packet sizes used by our shard transfer protocol.
- Secondary cause: aggressive conntrack/NAT timeout defaults on the customer's edge NAT (idle timeout 15s) combined with our client-side keepalive gaps caused ephemeral sessions to be torn during long model pulls, surfacing as EIO/connection reset errors in the loader.
- Contributing factor: Calico CNI configuration was using "vxlan" with an MTU not reconciled with host MTU; no automated MTU sanity-check in the install checklist.

Temporary mitigations applied during the sprint:
- Disabled jumbo frames on the appliance NICs (Jonah) — immediate reduction in packet fragmentation.
- Increased NAT idle timeout to 5 minutes on customer NAT gateway (Elena + network team) — reduced mid-transfer session tears.
- Added a loader retry loop with exponential backoff to the on-prem agent (Ava) — reduced visible 502s while shims in network layer were stabilized.

Permanent fix plan (accepted by customer):
- Short term (<=2 weeks): add MTU auto-detection to our install script and warn if fabric MTU != host MTU; ship patch 0.9.3 with loader keepalive improvements.
- Medium term (<=8 weeks): update deployment docs + runbook to include MTU sanity checks and NAT conntrack guidance; create a preflight check that probes for fragmentation behavior.
- Long term (<=6 months): add a transfer protocol variant that chunks large model artifacts at application layer to avoid reliance on jumbo frames entirely; validate on typical on‑prem fabrics.

Runbook and tooling changes (immediate edits):
- Deploy runbook update: "preflight-networking-mtu-and-nat.md" — new checklist items: check host NIC MTU, CNI MTU, edge switch config, and NAT idle timeout. (owner: Carlos, due 2027-11-10)
- Add automated tracer to install agent to surface fragmentation statistics during artifact pulls (owner: Ava, due 2027-11-17).
- Quick diagnostic: new one-liner to test fragmentation: `curl --data-binary @large.bin --header 'X-Test-Chunk: 8192' <appliance-ip>/diag/frag-check` (Jonah validated). Add to KB.

Decisions made:
- We will not force jumbo frame disable by default; install will detect mismatch and prompt operator with clear remediation steps. Customer education preferred to unilateral changes.
- Keep the loader retry/backoff shipped as a bandaid; it's expected to be short-lived once MTU detection and upstream guidance are live.

Open risks and unknowns:
- Edge vendors with broken MTU reporting may still misconfigure fabric; installer probe will need heuristics (e.g., active fragmentation test).
- Some customers configure intermediate L4 devices with their own timeouts; we need a recommended profile for popular NAT/appliances and include vendor notes.
- There is a small risk our application-layer chunking impacts cold-start latency for tiny models — will need careful perf testing.

Action items (owner, due):
- Carlos Mendes: Draft MTU and NAT guidance doc with vendor footnotes (Cisco/Arista/Juniper) — due 2027-11-10.
- Ava Chen: Ship loader keepalive + retry patch and add agent tracing hooks — due 2027-11-12.
- Jonah Patel: Add fragmentation diagnostic one-liners to KB and installer preflight script prototype — due 2027-11-08.
- Priya Nair: Coordinate customer comms and shared timeline; confirm SLA credit eligibility with CS — due 2027-11-06.
- Elena Gomez: Validate the patch with Acadia on staging and confirm NAT idle timeout change schedule — due 2027-11-07.

Notes for future installs:
- Add a short "networking deep dive" slide to standard install packet; call out MTU parity as a red flag.
- Consider adding an optional "artifact-proxy" component for customers who cannot change edge NAT behavior; keeps artifact transfers on internal LAN.

Appendix (debug traces and snippets):
- Example kernel dmesg during fragmentation: `frag: cannot defragment: skb_cow failing at offset 0x1f4`
- Loader error seen: `ERROR model_loader.go:212: rpc read: connection reset by peer (EIO)`
- Quick perf note: disabling jumbo frames reduced model pull tail latency from 1.6s to 0.4s per parallel stream in controlled test.

If anything is missing or you have more logs to attach, drop them into the linked Confluence page (Confluence:deploy-templates#acadia) and ping #field-acadia. We will re-run the install preflight checklist on Nov 8 in the morning shift and publish a short summary after validation.

-- Priya
